title: Innovative Dummy Variable Transformation for Modeling Deterministic Structural Shocks in Stationary Time Series in Cash Pooling
content: In cash pooling during corporate treasury management, it is important to predict cash inflows and outflows in specific responsibility centers, whether they will be predictable, and which cash management model will best describe them. Standard econometric models lose their forecasting accuracy exactly 12 months after a significant economic shock. This accuracy drift results from a mathematical error of double counting shock information in seasonally delayed variables and traditional binary variables. In this article, we solve this problem by introducing an innovative transformation of the binary variable value that dynamically adapts to the autoregressive parameters of the model (Molapo, et al., 2019). We tested our method on 330 models (SARMA, ARCH, GARCH). Our calculations, automated using proprietary scripts in the EViews environment, prove that the use of the transformation not only restores the reliability of long-term forecasts, but also significantly increases the stability of stationary processes. We have shown that models equipped with the new transformation retain their stationary properties in over 91% of cases (for ARCH models), outperforming the traditional approach. The presented method is a ready-made tool for analysts and chief financial officers (CFOs), allowing for precise liquidity planning and corporate treasury management in conditions of structural uncertainty. The paper describes the procedure for modeling a deterministic structural shock. The three mathematical sciences are combined in the paper: statistics, numerical methods, and econometrics, so all the calculations must have been coded. All the calculations were coded in EViews. The paper shows that our approach models structural shock in an innovative way, but it also causes models to represent stationary processes.
